note: Positive and defeating cases for contracts/verification-budget.json. The rule under test is decisions/0074: a wall-clock reading records debt and never refuses, a check over its own ceiling is attributed and never refuses, and exactly one timing condition blocks - a single check past catastrophic_check_seconds. B-004 through B-007 are the defeating cases: each is a way the old global gate would have refused a run that this table must let pass, or a way the new table could quietly stop applying pressure at all. Times are in seconds and are inputs to the judge, not measurements of anything.

cases.proves: Every check inside its ceiling and a wall time inside the fastest band produces no debt, and the run says so rather than staying silent.
3.5s is seven times the 0.5s default and would be debt under it. The named 4.0s ceiling is what this check answers to.
A check added without a ceiling is not thereby exempt. The default applies and its overrun is attributed by name.

The defeating case for the old gate. 24.7s is a measured loaded-host reading that decisions/0050 would have failed outright. It earns no grade and records wall-clock debt; it produces no catastrophe and nothing here refuses.
The measured 2026-08-27 state. Both checks owe debt, both are named, and neither refuses the run - so a change to an unrelated fast check lands while the debt stays visible against its owner.
The one timing condition that still blocks. Without this case the table would apply no hard pressure anywhere and a suite could grow without limit.
One regression is reported once. The catastrophic check is over its 4.0s ceiling too, and must not appear in both lists; its sibling's ordinary debt is unaffected.
